name: Staekske Rape
description: Staekske Rape (Limburgish: 'Pick Up the Stock') is a Dutch Jass game played in Maastricht and surrounding areas. It is played by four players with a 32-card deck (7s through Aces), featuring a bidding process where the winner takes the 4-card 'Stock' and names trumps. It combines trick-taking with meld declarations ('Stoek' and 'Vier' - 4 of a kind, sequence of 3+).
deck: 32 cards (Standard Piquet deck or Dutch/French suits).

history.origins: Dates to the 19th century as a local variant of Klaverjassen/Jass. The name is dialect for 'Stock Grabbing'.
history.cultural: Highly regional; rules vary by village.
history.evolution: The bidding system (2-Blind, 3, 4, 5...) is unique to this variant.

setup.players: Four players (or five with dealer sitting out each hand).
setup.deck: 32 cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in clubs, spades, hearts, diamonds (French or Dutch indices).
setup.dealing: First dealer: deal face-up clockwise until someone receives a jack. Then shuffle, player to dealer's right cuts. Deal clockwise: 3 cards to each player, 4 face-down in centre (stock), then 4 cards to each player. Everyone has 7 cards.

rules.objective: As declarer, take at least the bid number of card points (in tricks plus stock and melds). Bids 3–6 mean 130–160+ points. Sitter forced to play if all pass (bid 1 = 110 points or concede for -10 game points).
rules.gameplay: After deal, bidding starts with player to dealer's left (sitter). First speaker is to sitter's left. Bid 3 or pass; then pass or next number (4, 5, 6…). No jump bids. Only first round allows blind 2 (without looking). Declarer takes 4-card stock, discards 4 face-down (or plays without stock for doubled stakes). Declarer announces melds (melles: four of a kind, sequences; stoek: K-Q of trumps) before first lead (sequences) or by when Q of trumps is played (stoek). Declarer names trumps and leads. Follow suit or trump; jack of trumps never forced. Trick to highest trump, else highest of led suit. Winner leads next. Seven tricks.
keyRules: Bidding: 3 = 130 pts, 4 = 140, 5 = 150, 6 = 160; pass or next number only.
Declarer takes stock and discards 4, or plays without stock (double stakes).
Sequences and fours announced before first lead; stoek (K-Q trumps) by Q of trumps.
Follow suit or trump; may trump anytime; never forced to play jack of trumps.
146 card points total (141 in cards + 5 for last trick); all seven tricks = +10 bonus.

strategy.basic: Bid only if you have a strong hand or can use the stock. The stock is 4 cards (12.5% of deck). It can make or break you. Count trumps carefully. The Jack (Jass) and Nine (Ninel) are critical.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Blind 2' Bid: A risky bid made without looking. Can pay off big if you hit.
strategy.advanced: Signaling: Discards can signal suit preference. Watch for partner's signals.

variations.name: Blind 2
variations.description: On first round only, a player may bid 2 without looking at cards (contract 120 points). Next bid over blind 2 must be 4, not 3.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Blind 2 only changes bidding options and contract; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Without stock
variations.description: Declarer may choose to play with original 7 cards without taking the stock. Card points in stock still count for declarer; game points won or lost are doubled.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Without stock only affects stakes (doubled) and declarer choice; no engine structure overrides.

scoring.description: Declarer wins or loses game points (1 game point ≈ 10 card points). Achieved: card points in tricks plus stock, rounded; +5 last trick; +10 bonus for all seven tricks. Required: bid + 10 minus (meld points ÷ 10). Win difference or lose 2×difference + 10; no stock doubles amount.
scoring.winCondition: Declarer must take at least the bid number of card points (tricks + stock + melds). Game points: achieved minus required; loss = 2×shortfall + 10.
